description: The plot titled “Massive Activation of baseline” illustrates how the maximum activation value varies by transformer layer for four baseline signals. The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately layers 0 to 23 with regularly spaced tick labels at about 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis is labeled “Max Activation Value,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0 up to about 1600 with evenly spaced tick labels (approximately every 200). Four lines are shown with a legend: a blue dashed line with small markers for “attn_output,” an orange dotted line with small markers for “attn_residual,” a green dash-dot line with small markers for “ffn_output,” and a red solid line for “ffn_residual.” The red solid “ffn_residual” stays near 0 through about layer 5, jumps to roughly 1400 around layer 6, remains near 1400–1600 across most mid-to-late layers, and then drops sharply near the final layers (ending around a few hundred). The orange dotted “attn_residual” is near 0 in early layers, rises sharply to around 1400 near layer 6, stays near that level for much of the remaining layers, and then declines near the end (ending below the plateau). The green dash-dot “ffn_output” is near 0 in early layers, shows a tall spike around layer 6 (near the top of the axis), then falls back close to 0 for many layers, with another prominent spike in the mid-to-late layers (around the mid-teens) before returning near 0 toward the end. The blue dashed “attn_output” remains close to 0 for most layers and then increases noticeably only near the last few layers, reaching a few hundred by the final layer.
